title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Development and Quality of Life

questions.prompt: Which indicator is the total value of goods and services produced divided by the population? (write the abbreviation with 'per capita')
Which THREE things does the HDI combine?
options: Birth rate, death rate and migration

questions.prompt: A country's GDP is R900 billion and its population is 30 million. Calculate the GDP per capita in rand.
A Gini coefficient close to 0 means a country is very unequal.
questions.explanation: 0 means perfect equality; values close to 1 mean great inequality.

questions.prompt: Match each indicator to the type of development it measures.
Give FOUR reasons why some countries remain less developed.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): colonial history; unfair trade/raw material exports; debt; natural disasters; disease; corruption/conflict; poor infrastructure; low education levels

questions.prompt: What does NGO stand for?
Food parcels given to flood victims are an example of…
What is the South African name for a community savings club?
One disadvantage of aid is that it can create dependency.
Match each programme to what it provides.
Explain how educating girls helps a country to develop.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): women earn higher incomes; healthier families/better child nutrition; lower birth rates; children more likely to attend school; more skilled workforce

questions.prompt: What is microfinance and how does it help development?
questions.memo:
✓ Small loans given to poor people without collateral (1)
✓ They can start or grow small businesses and earn an income (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Surface Forces: Weathering and Erosion

questions.prompt: What is the breaking down of rock in place called?
Frost action is a type of…
Chemical weathering is fastest in hot, wet climates.
Match each landform to the agent that formed it.
Explain how freeze–thaw weathering breaks rocks.
questions.memo:
✓ Water enters cracks in the rock (1)
✓ At night it freezes and expands, widening the crack (1)
✓ Repeated freezing and thawing eventually breaks the rock apart (1)

questions.prompt: Explain ONE way in which living things weather rocks.
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. plant roots grow in cracks and push them apart / lichens produce acids / animals burrow and expose rock (2 for a clear explanation)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Landforms, Mass Movement and Soil Erosion

questions.prompt: A flat-topped hill that is wider than it is high is a…
Waterfalls and V-shaped valleys are typical of a river's…
What South African word describes a deep gully caused by soil erosion?
Ploughing up and down a slope helps prevent soil erosion.
questions.explanation: Contour ploughing, along the slope, slows water flow.

questions.prompt: Match each landform to its course.
Explain how a meander changes shape over time.
questions.memo:
✓ Water flows fastest on the outside of the bend and erodes a river cliff (1)
✓ Water is slowest on the inside and deposits sediment (slip-off slope) (1)
✓ The bend becomes bigger and may be cut off to form an oxbow lake (1)

questions.prompt: Name TWO factors that can trigger a landslide.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): heavy rain; earthquakes; removing vegetation; building/cutting into slopes; mining; undercutting by rivers or waves
